title: Enlarged etale ringed-site models of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with sites chosen small relative to the universe of sheaves as in [def-weil-size-convention]. For morphisms $a:A\to B$ of algebraic spaces, use etale in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale morphism $U\to A$ from a scheme, the composite $U\to B$ is representable etale (representable etale has the scheme-test meaning of [def-trf-algebraic-space]). Let $\mathcal C_X$ have as objects etale morphisms $T\to X$ from algebraic spaces over $S$, as morphisms the maps over $X$, and as coverings the jointly surjective etale families [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Restriction along the inclusion $X_{\mathrm{et}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal C_X$ of scheme objects is an equivalence of sheaf topoi. A sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ has an extension $\widetilde F$ to $\mathcal C_X$, unique up to unique isomorphism restricting to the identity on $F$; for a surjective etale scheme chart $T_0\to T$, its sections are the equalizer $\widetilde F(T)=\operatorname{Eq}(F(T_0)\rightrightarrows F(T_0\times_TT_0))$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], naturally in $T$ and $F$. This extends the structure sheaf and gives an equivalence of categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for $\mathcal O_X$ and its extension $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X$. For every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, the functor $v_f:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$, $V\mapsto X\times_YV$, is continuous and defines the small etale morphism of topoi under these equivalences. With the ring map induced on scheme charts by pullback of regular functions, this is the canonical morphism of ringed topoi for $f$; these constructions are compatible with composition. For every etale morphism $u:Z'\to Z$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, postcomposition identifies $\mathcal C_{Z'}$ with the localized site $\mathcal C_Z/Z'$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with the same coverings, and identifies $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_{Z'}$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_Z|_{Z'}$. Under these identifications the morphism of ringed topoi for $u$ is the localization morphism.

proof.text: Implementation-level foundations and reductions for the published enlarged-site module: a representable scheme sheaf has representable diagonal by the Yoneda relative-representability criterion, and its identity is a surjective etale atlas. A scheme small-site object is chartwise etale by composition of representable etale maps. Chartwise etale composition follows directly by applying the two defining predicates successively. For base change of a chartwise etale object, pull a scheme atlas of its source back to the sheaf fibre product. Cancel pullback squares to identify its composite to the new base as the base change of the chartwise-etale atlas composite. Apply [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection] to descend from this representable surjective etale cover. For an atlas self-overlap, apply its representable-etale scheme test along itself. The resulting etale scheme projection makes the overlap an object of the small site, using [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]; Yoneda lifts the other projection and faithful limit reflection gives the pullback in the enlarged site. Extension existence and normalized uniqueness follow from the restriction equivalence: use its counit for existence, and lift e followed by the inverse of d through full faithfulness for uniqueness. Transport an enlarged geometric morphism through the two restriction equivalences by composing the three adjunctions; the inverse images remain left exact. These arguments discharge these implementation clauses without invoking the comparison packets below. The atlas is a singleton cover: each surjective scheme test has a point whose residue field defines a field-extension lift. Apply the singleton-cover sheaf gluing condition to the displayed pullback square and transport the compatible sections through the given restriction isomorphism; separatedness proves injectivity, and unique gluing proves surjectivity with the required restriction formula. Finally, postcomposition factors as the stated covering-preserving localization equivalence followed by the slice forgetful functor. Both factors are continuous, hence so is postcomposition. The site axioms and finite limits are now proved directly in the enlarged-site module: chartwise cancellation is proved by the scheme-test comparison and source-atlas detection; the actual sheaf pullbacks give enlarged pullbacks. Field-extension lifting proves covering identities, composition, and arbitrary covering pullback, including empty families. Scheme-point surjectivity agrees with field-extension lifting by residue-field tests and points of scheme pullbacks. Yoneda full faithfulness and preservation of these explicit scheme pullbacks then give continuity of scheme inclusion. These local proved subarguments reuse the source proofs of scheme density without importing its downstream module. Base change agrees with ambient slice pullback under a fully faithful finite-limit-preserving inclusion, hence preserves finite limits. Pullback of covering field-valued sections proves covering preservation, and the covering-equalizer criterion proves continuity. Flat left Kan extension followed by sheafification is the left exact left adjoint, proving enlargedDirectImage_geometric. For identity, construct the projection comparison X times_X V to V, and apply enlargedStructuralMap_existsUnique to the restriction map induced by this projection. On every commuting scheme triangle its composite with enlargedChartLift is exactly the scheme-inclusion map; naturality of the normalization and its inverse identity prove the prescribed ordinary pullback formula. No structural-map existence or restriction-equivalence hole is used to prove site axioms, continuity, or the geometric morphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-enlarged-atlas-algebraic-extension] to any space $A$. Its normalized extension gives $\widetilde F$, uniqueness, and the specified atlas equalizer naturally in $T$ and $F$. For each space under consideration, choose once its normalized ring extension at $R=\mathcal O_A$; use these same extensions in steps 3 and 4. At $A=X$ this gives $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X$ and the asserted module-category equivalence.

proof.text: For f:X to Y, the actual fibre-product functor is proved continuous and finite-limit-preserving by step 1. Flat left Kan extension and sheafification give enlargedDirectImage_geometric, and enlargedSmallDirectImage_geometric transports it along the published restriction equivalences. The remaining canonical structural-map existence and its regular-function normalization follow the normalized ring-extension and chart-descent argument of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-atlas-algebraic-extension] and [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism]; those structural clauses are not discharged in this partial delivery.

proof.text: For every composable pair, the direct-image formulas and chart-normalized structural maps obtained in step 3 satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization]; its adjunction-compatible comparisons therefore give composition with the structural ring maps. Its projection-preserving identity comparisons satisfy the unit laws, and its three-map comparisons give associativity, including the structural ring maps. For etale $u:Z'\to Z$, apply its postcomposition equivalence, which preserves exactly the coverings. Under this equivalence the normalized identification $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_Z|_{Z'}\simeq\widetilde{\mathcal O}_{Z'}$ is the identity on scheme sections. The same cited statement identifies the inverse image with restriction, the direct image at $V$ with $G(V\times_ZZ'\to Z')$, and the structural map with this ring identification. Thus all three data of the ringed morphism agree with localization. The identity clause is now proved directly from the canonical structural-map uniqueness theorem by the projection and chart calculation in step 1; composition and localization remain the stated route and remain unproved here.
